title: Hosted Inference Bundle: PRD + Launch Readiness Playbook (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank)
creator: Ethan Wang
body:
Summary:
This PRD defines the product and launch-readiness criteria for the 'Hosted Inference Bundle' — a cohesive hosted API surface that ships chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints as a single, discoverable product offering. The goal is to provide a consistent developer contract, clear performance SLAs, straightforward migration paths from experimental endpoints, and an operational playbook for safe rollout and rollback.

Goals and success metrics:
- Developer adoption: 10% of new API signups use at least one bundle endpoint in first 30 days post-launch.
- Latency & availability: P99 generation latency for short-prompt chat/completions <= 300ms (single-token steady-state), availability >= 99.95% for GA customers.
- Cost predictability: Provide clear unit-cost documentation and per-token billing that aligns with existing hosted pricing.
- Reliability: Zero-severity incidents introduced by new surface in first 30 days; any regressions must have automated rollbacks.
- Quality guardrails: No more than 2% quality regressions vs. baseline prompts for each model family at GA (as measured by agreed eval suites).

Scope (what's in):
- Expose four first-class endpoints in the hosted API product: /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank.
- Single model catalog entry type with version pinning and variant mapping (quantized variants, fallback variants).
- Streaming and non-streaming responses for chat and completions.
- Structured output support (schema validation hooks) for chat/completions.
- Embeddings API with batching and vector normalization options.
- Rerank API that accepts candidate lists and returns scores + ranked indices.
- Console pages showing per-route latency, cost breakdown, and failure trends.
- Canary rollout mechanism: percentage-based traffic toggles, automatic metric gating.

Out of scope (for this release):
- Multi-modal (image/vision) endpoints.
- Dedicated/Dedicated-only private deployment flows (the bundle must work in Hosted; Dedicated follow-ups will adapt).
- Deep policy for custom model hosting; this release supports Redwood-curated models only.

User personas & key user stories:
- ML/Backend Engineer: "I want predictable throughput and simple API contracts so my service can call a single endpoint for generation or embedding and keep latency under SLOs."
- Product Engineer: "I want console visibility and cost breakdown by route so I can justify usage costs to stakeholders."
- Platform Operator (Redwood): "I need clear rollout gates and automated rollback triggers to protect SLOs during launch."

API surface overview (developer-facing):
- Chat: conversation-oriented call, message array input, streaming tokens, function/tool-calling metadata.
- Completions: prompt-based single-call generation, streaming optional, stop sequences and max_tokens controls.
- Embeddings: single/batch text input, dimension-detected, optional normalization and pooling.
- Rerank: inputs: query + list of candidate texts or ids; outputs: scores, normalized rank, optional explain tokens.

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Backwards compatible parameter aliases: support legacy param names for 6 months with deprecation warnings in responses.
- Model alias mapping: provide mapping table between legacy endpoint model names and new catalog names.
- Throttling and quotas: existing quota system applies; introduce per-route quotas for heavy rerank/embedding workloads with guidance for burst allowances.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- See acceptance_criteria field for a checklist of machine-readable acceptance items and numeric SLOs.

Operational runbook (rollout & rollback summary):
- Phase 1 (internal canary): 5% traffic from internal customers + staging; run for 48 hours with metric gating.
- Phase 2 (invite-only beta): 20% external customers (opt-in) for 7 days; allow manual hold.
- Phase 3 (gradual GA): increment by 20% per day with automated gating; full GA after 5 successful days.
- Automated rollback triggers: sustained P99 latency 2x baseline for 10 minutes or error rate > 1% on any route for 5 minutes.

Telemetry & observability requirements:
- Per-route metrics: requests/min, tokens/sec, token cost unit, p50/p95/p99 latency (generation and total), error counts by status code, stream drop rate.
- Per-model metrics: average KV cache hit rate, average sequence length, batching efficiency.
- Tracing: correlate API request -> runtime node -> kernel selection.
- Synthetic checks: run canonical prompt set for each endpoint every 30 minutes and record quality and latency.
- Alerts: SLO burn rate alert integrations (PagerDuty) for P99 breaches.

Security & compliance:
- TLS mandatory; mutual-TLS for any partner-facing invite-only beta.
- KMS integration for persisted logs in private regions; hosted logs must be redacted per PII policy.
- Security review required pre-GA (see security_review_required=true).

Quality and evaluation plan:
- Maintain accepted prompt sets per endpoint and run nightly evals comparing baseline model performance to release candidate.
- Acceptance threshold: automated quality score must not regress beyond 2% relative to baseline across golden prompt sets per model.
- Human review sampling: 500 randomly sampled generations/day for first week of GA.

Dependencies and risks:
- ENG-1842: SDK streaming library completion (blocking for streaming clients).
- ENG-2910: Runtime kernel selector updates to ensure quantized variant parity.
- UX risk: console cost breakdown UI delayed could reduce transparency and increase support load.
- Model drift: quality regressions if runtime picks an incompatible kernel; mitigated by canary model pinning.

Rollout notes for support and comms:
- Developer announcement: blog post + docs + API samples and migration guide.
- Customer comms: targeted emails to larger customers with guidance on quotas and performance expectations.
- Internal: runbook and playbook distributed to SRE/Support with on-call rotation and escalation paths.

Open questions and deferred decisions:
- Whether to expose fine-grained caching controls to customers in GA or keep cache management internal. (Default: internal; evaluate in GA.)
- Exact pricing tiers for rerank heavy workloads — will finalize after 2-week beta.

References and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Hosted+Inference+Bundle+PRD
- API contract draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/hosted-api-contract-draft
- Design mocks: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/design/hosted-bundle
- Eval dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-bundle-evals
acceptance_criteria: API contracts implemented for /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank with documented request/response schemas
Streaming for chat and completions functions end-to-end (SDK + HTTP SSE) verified with integration tests and sample apps
Per-route P99 latency <= 300ms for baseline short prompts in us-east-1 (synthetic load)
Availability >= 99.95% measured across GA traffic for 30-day rolling window
Rerank and embeddings support batching and per-request timeout semantics; tests cover large-candidate inputs
Console pages show per-route latency and spend breakdown prior to public GA
Automatic canary gating and rollback hooks wired into deployment pipeline; tests simulate rollback triggers
Security review completed and any action items closed or scoped into follow-up release
Migration guide published and legacy param aliases supported with deprecation warnings
Quality evals show <= 2% regression across golden prompt sets for each model family
rollout_checklist: Run internal canary (5% internal traffic) for 48h: collect metrics and signoff
Invite-only beta for 7 days with monitoring and weekly syncs with participating customers
Enable console cost dashboards and make docs public on docs.redwood.ai
Update SDKs: JavaScript, Python streaming examples with feature flags
Perform PD/IR tabletop for rollback scenarios with SRE and Support
Publish migration guide and model alias table
Confirm KMS and logging redaction settings for hosted regions
Set up synthetic prompt runs and alerting (Grafana + PagerDuty)
Security review signoff from Security team
Create post-launch monitoring plan and retrospective date scheduled
